title: Jumbo Jets Find New Life as Hotel Suites
paragraphs: The Boeing 747, often called the "jumbo jet," carried millions of passengers around the world for more than 50 years. Now, two old 747s in Malaysia have a new job: they have become hotel rooms.

The hotel is called 1975 Avenue & Hotel, and it is in Johor Bahru, in the south of Malaysia, near Singapore. According to reports, it opened in August 2026. The hotel has turned two old planes into 18 suites, with nine suites in each plane. There are also 20 normal rooms in a building next to the planes.

Both planes have long histories. One was built in 1970 and flew for the American airline Pan Am. Later, it was changed into a cargo plane, and it ended up in Malaysia. The other plane flew for Japan Airlines from 1980 to 1998. It was a special type of 747 for short flights in Japan, and it could carry up to 533 passengers. The plane was taken apart and moved to the hotel site in 2019.

There are four types of suites, and each suite has the theme of a different country, such as Japan, Korea, Mexico or Italy. The biggest suites have two floors, a bedroom, a living room and a large bathtub. The hotel is about 20 minutes by car from Senai International Airport. It also has a man-made beach, swimming pools, a spa, a gym and restaurants.
The suites are not cheap. Earlier in 2026, prices for the plane suites were about 1,500 to 3,000 Malaysian ringgit per night.
Other old planes have also become hotels. For example, a 747 at Stockholm's airport in Sweden was a hotel for many years, but it closed in 2025.
